title: SecOps-NG Sovereignty Posture Evidence Artifact
description: Typed shape for one evidence artifact emitted by the sovereignty evidence stream (F-SV-04). One artifact attests the sovereign posture over a declared assessment window: one observation per sovereignty-cluster indicator from content/metrics/ (every indicator, mechanically — the observations object requires all of them, so a record cannot silently under-report the posture it attests to) plus an attestation state drawn from the shared four-state vocabulary in schemas/attestation_state.json. Deliberately carries NO numeric aggregate: a single sovereignty score invites the claim 'N% sovereign', which is not a defensible statement — the same reasoning that keeps a percentage out of the SOC 2 readiness attestation. The record is composed from observations the operator supplies; it names no sink and carries no endpoint literal, so the artifact cannot itself become a non-EU reference that kri.hardcoded_non_eu_endpoint_reference_count@v1 would count.

schema_version.description: Pinned schema version. Lets a consumer reject artifacts produced under an older schema once breaking changes ship.

artifact_id.description: Stable per-artifact identifier. Convention: SHA-256 hex digest of `<workflow_id>|<execution_id>|<compile_target>` (UTF-8, no separators around the pipes). Deterministic on those three inputs so a replay of the same execution under the same compile target re-derives the same id.

stream.description: Identifies which evidence stream produced the artifact. Constant on this schema.

workflow_id.description: Stable identifier of the workflow whose execution composed this artifact. Convention: lower-snake-case workflow stable-id from `content/playbooks/<workflow>/`.

execution_id.description: Per-execution identifier issued by the compile target's workflow runtime (n8n execution id, Temporal workflow run id, LangGraph thread/checkpoint id).

compile_target.description: Which of the three reference compile targets produced the running form of the workflow. Constrained to the three reference targets the project ships compilers for.

regulation_refs.description: Pins to the upstream regulatory mapping entries the attested posture bears on (typically GDPR Chapter V transfer atoms and NIS2 Art. 21(2)(d) supply-chain atoms — the sovereignty indicators' own external_refs are the authority). At least one entry: an artifact with no regulatory anchor is not evidence in the F-CP sense.

control_refs.description: Control stable-ids the attested posture evidences. Same shape every other layer of the content model uses.

assessment_window.description: The window the observations cover. Observations sampled at different instants inside the window are legitimate; the window bounds are the honesty contract about how stale the oldest observation may be.

from.description: ISO-8601 UTC start of the assessment window.

to.description: ISO-8601 UTC end of the assessment window.

observations.description: One observation per sovereignty-cluster indicator, keyed by the indicator's stable_id. Every indicator carrying `foundation_property: sovereignty` under content/metrics/ is REQUIRED and no other key is accepted — completeness is schema-enforced so the record cannot silently under-report, and a new sovereignty-tagged indicator must be added here (test_sovereignty_evidence_schema.py fails naming the metric until it is). Deliberately an exhaustive enumeration rather than a pattern: the point is that this list and the catalogue can never drift apart silently.

attestation_state.description: State of this posture attestation, drawn from the shared four-state vocabulary (schemas/attestation_state.json) — reused by $ref, never redeclared. This is a categorical state about the attestation exercise (fresh and complete vs. gapped vs. overdue), NOT a sovereignty verdict and NOT a score; per-indicator evaluation against a declared baseline is the F-SV-05 conformance profile's job.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which this artifact was composed. Not part of `artifact_id` — re-emissions inside the same execution stay byte-identical at the path level.

provenance.description: Where this artifact came from. Mirrors the provenance pattern used by content/controls/*.yaml so a reviewer can re-derive the chain back to source.

source_url.description: URL of the workflow run (or workflow-content source) that produced this artifact. Compile targets may use their own run-id URLs; the URL itself is opaque to this schema.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 date or date-time matching the artifact-level captured_at.

commit_sha.description: Optional commit SHA of the content snapshot the workflow walked.

observation.description: One indicator observation: the value observed inside the assessment window and the threshold band it fell in, per the indicator's own catalogue thresholds. No aggregate is derived from these — the record carries the observations, the F-SV-05 profile carries the judgement.

observed_value.description: The indicator reading (ratio, rate, or cardinality — the indicator's catalogue entry declares the unit).

threshold_band.description: The band the observed value fell in against the indicator's own catalogue thresholds. `on_target` means no threshold fired.

observed_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant this indicator was sampled. Must fall inside the artifact's assessment_window; the window, not this field, is the staleness contract.
